## Problem

A merged release PR integrates a prepared version but cannot publish it — the
annotated `v<version>` tag is the sole publication intent. Nothing mechanically
notices when that tag never arrives. The integrated version then sits silently
in `awaiting-tag`, and the next shipped-file PR happily prepares the *next*
version on top of it.

Observed 2026-07-25: 0.34.2 was merged in the morning and never tagged. Later
the same day the #231 PR prepared 0.34.3 on top of it. Nothing anywhere went
red. Both versions ended up published by one `v0.34.3` tag, which means 0.34.2
never existed as its own release artifact even though its release-notes section
claims it does. The drift was caught only because a human asked "are you done
with everything".

Two smaller findings from the same incident:

- The tag-triggered run went red on `TLOG_CREATE_ENTRY_ERROR` (Sigstore
  transparency log 409) and, on the recovery dispatch, on the known npm
  readback race (#205) — publish had succeeded both times.
- `npm run release:status` reported `awaiting-npm` while the package was
  already on the registry, because `npm pack <spec>` served a **stale local
  packument cache** (`ETARGET`). A status command that can silently misreport a
  published release as unpublished is a real defect: acting on it would mean
  re-publishing.

## Proposal

Close the stacking hole where a human is present anyway — PR time.

`scripts/release-delta-guard.mjs` already runs on every PR in CI and inside
`/local-ci`. Extend `assessRelease` with one rule: when a PR raises the version
(`currentVersion !== baseVersion`), the **base** version must already carry its
annotated tag. Otherwise fail with the concrete previous version and the exact
recovery step.

Keep it honest at the edges:

- Resolve the tag prefix from the release profile, never a hardcoded `v`; the
  guard ships to consumers with their own tagging vocabulary.
- Skip the rule for a repository that has no matching tag at all (bootstrap /
  never-released repo) — the rule guards *stacking*, not first release.
- The rule stays a pure-function check with its facts passed in, so
  `scripts/release-delta-guard.test.mjs` can cover it without touching git.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A PR that bumps the version while the base version has no matching
      annotated tag fails `release:guard` with a message naming the untagged
      version and the recovery step.
- [ ] A PR that bumps the version when the base version IS tagged passes
      unchanged; a PR with no shipped delta is unaffected.
- [ ] A repository with no matching tags at all is not blocked (bootstrap
      escape), and the tag prefix comes from the release profile.
- [ ] `release-state.mjs` cannot report `awaiting-npm` off a stale local
      packument cache — the registry read is cache-bypassing, with a test.
- [ ] The release doctrine in `CLAUDE.md` and the `kit-release` skill (both
      surfaces) state the new guard and that a red release run still requires
      the `npm view` / `gh release view` check before reacting.
response.title: release: block a version bump while the previous release is still awaiting-tag

## Problem

The release doctrine demands **two** human gates: one to confirm the Semver used
to prepare the metadata, and a second, separate confirmation after merge before
the annotated tag may be created. The maintainer does not want to perform the
second step at all — tagging is the agent's job:

> "ich werde nicht taggen, das muss der agent machen das muss irgendwo
> hinterlegt sein"

Today the opposite is written in five places: `CLAUDE.md:106`, the `kit-release`
skill description and its step 5 on **both** surfaces, and
`docs/adr/0004-release-intent-is-a-version-tag.md:46`. So every release stalls
at `awaiting-tag` until a human returns — which is exactly how 0.34.2 was
skipped and buried under 0.34.3 (#243).

## Decision

**The confirmed Semver authorizes the whole release, through tag and publish.**
One gate, at the moment the version is chosen, instead of two. After that the
agent merges, creates and pushes the annotated tag, monitors the workflow, and
reports parity — without asking again.

What does **not** change:

- The tag stays the sole publication intent; merging still only integrates.
- Every existing gate before it stays hard: guard, staleness, full suite, pack,
  and the workflow's own tag/version/ancestry validation.
- A red release run still requires reconstructing real state (`npm view`,
  `gh release view`) before reacting, and recovery is still the idempotent
  reconciler on the existing tag — never a new version.
- Publication remains irreversible: npm versions cannot be reused. The
  authorization moves earlier; it does not disappear.

## Scope

`kit-release` is **maintainer-only**: its two surfaces plus
`scripts/kit-release.mjs` and `scripts/release-delta-guard.mjs` carry
`installRole: maintainer` — 4 of 326 manifest entries — and
`scripts/build-kit.test.mjs:63` asserts a consumer `init` never installs them.
The policy therefore lives directly in the skill; no consumer inherits it and no
profile key is needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both `kit-release` surfaces state that the confirmed Semver carries
      through to tag and publish, and neither asks for a separate confirmation
      before tagging.
- [ ] The skill still names the irreversibility and every pre-tag gate.
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` carry the same doctrine, with the old
      two-gate wording gone.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0004-release-intent-is-a-version-tag.md` records the change as
      a dated amendment rather than a silent rewrite.
- [ ] A contract test pins the new wording on both surfaces and fails if the
      second-confirmation requirement returns.

# Program: Simplify the session-end lifecycle (green slate)

## Problem

Fifteen teardown/cleanup issues in two weeks (#245–#319). The provenance-bound
teardown machinery (ADR-0007) grew to ~5,800 lines (5,822 counted: scripts/worktree-lifecycle/* + wrapup-land.py, wc -l 2026-07-27) with two recovery flags for
its own bookkeeping, and routine sessions could no longer finish: an unseeded
`scratchPatterns` made teardown impossible (#319), a planning session had no
landing door at all (#317, #318). Each fix added a guard layer; each layer
produced the next issue.

## Solution

Green slate per **ADR-0009** (supersedes ADR-0007): teardown authority is
Stateless teardown classification — git's own file taxonomy over the standard
exclude sources plus the platform PR record, read at the moment of action.
`.env*` is the single hardcoded exception (compared against the main
checkout). wrapup gains the Content route for planning sessions; worktree
creation binds to implementation; external worktrees are first-class and
`/wrapup` always lands **and** tears down. The provenance core (receipts,
journals, frozen attempts, recovery flags, artifact baseline) is removed
without migration; deletion policy has exactly one configuration surface: the
ignore mechanism. Safety floor unchanged: no tracked-work loss, no commits on
the protected branch, no force bypasses, no silent deletion. The full locked
spec is the grill + 5-round Codex-approved plan (39 findings incorporated);
its durable decisions live in ADR-0009 and CONTEXT.md (Stateless teardown
classification, Scratch, Durable content, Content route).

Throughout: "`main`" is shorthand for the profile's configured protected
branch — no command, test, or prose may hardcode the literal name. The
program's acceptance gate is **zero references to removed machinery in
executable or current-contract surfaces**; historical evidence (superseded
ADR-0007, release notes, review logs) is an explicit listed allowlist.

## Scope

- **S1:** Stateless classification core: four rules from
  `git status --porcelain=v2 -z` (tracked-modified blocks; untracked
  non-ignored blocks with bounded report; ignored = Scratch, deletable;
  `.env*` no-follow byte-compare against the main checkout), no-follow
  deletion primitive, one capped deterministic report schema for every
  category.
- **S2:** Provenance machinery removed: session.py claim/receipt/proof-ref/
  patch-index/seal/recover paths, landing-attempt journal, both recovery
  flags, v1/v2 receipt contracts, canonical policy reload, artifact-baseline
  machinery — old on-disk journals become inert.
- **S3:** Branch deletion authorized by the PR record: full tuple (base repo,
  head repo = base repo, head ref, base ref = protected branch, `MERGED`,
  uniqueness, no open PR on head) + tip-OID re-read before deletion;
  owner-qualified historical query for interrupted runs; `land --pr <n>`
  first-class fallback; fresh-fetch ancestry, stale ancestry stops.
- **S4:** wrapup lands and tears down any worktree: external worktrees
  first-class (foreign paths/branch names), detached HEAD / unborn branch =
  named STOP, issue anchor optional, process kill scoped to `.dev-ports`
  listeners bound under the worktree (pidfd where available; never signal on
  doubt).
- **S5:** Content route: a planning session with no worktree lands durable
  content from the main checkout — inferred, one-gate explicit file claim
  with per-path hash verification, same `.env` hard block + secret scan,
  collision-checked issue-less branch, `Part of #<anchor>` never `closes`,
  no teardown half, authorization unchanged (user-only).
- **S6:** Profile/schema cut: `scratchPatterns` +
  `landingGeneratedArtifactPatterns` removed from schema, setup-workflow and
  the shipped 0.38.0 consumer migration (no migration code, old keys
  ignored); new schema-contracted issue-less content branch template key.
- **S7:** to-issues end state + worktree discipline: post-publication
  two-line state report naming the exact next step (`/wrapup`), never
  deletes; worktree binds to implementation, not planning (CLAUDE.md + grill
  skills).
- **S8:** Shipped-surface consistency: counted census over every executable/
  current-contract surface (bundle manifest, package file list, capabilities
  schema, consumer-migrations, skills on both surfaces, CLAUDE.md,
  CONTEXT.md, profile-glob tooling, tests) with the zero-stale-references
  acceptance gate and explicit historical allowlist.
- **S10:** Census freshness gets a session-end home: wrapup consults
  `--census-status` as a named step — `ok` silent; `refresh_required` becomes a
  named session-end finding stating verdict, reason, the **evaluated checkout**
  (worktree vs. main — a worktree-green verdict never masks a stale main), and
  the consumer-prescribed recovery route (dedicated chore PR, never a file
  mirror); optionally (consumer-configurable) a tracking issue so the finding
  survives the session. Explicit non-goal: no hard gate on the feature PR
  (#321).
- **S9:** Documentation refresh — deliberately the **last** wave: README and
  the GitHub Pages site under `docs/`, including the lifecycle

## Problem

`to-waves` carries `disable-model-invocation: true`, but the public Planning
facade `to-issues` **delegates to it by contract** ("Program identity →
delegate to the internal `to-waves` graph engine"). The agent therefore cannot
load the engine through the Skill tool mid-run:

```
Skill to-waves cannot be used with Skill tool due to disable-model-invocation
```

Observed 2026-07-27 during the `/to-issues` run on Program-PRD #320: the facade
had to fall back to reading `SKILL.md` by hand. That works but bypasses the
Skill loader (no directory-scoped variant resolution, no consistent invocation
telemetry) and contradicts the facade design: an internal engine a public
skill routes into must be loadable by the model.

## What to change

- Remove `disable-model-invocation: true` from
  `.claude/skills/to-waves/SKILL.md` frontmatter so the facade can invoke it.
- Keep the routing discipline in prose/description: normal entry stays
  `/to-issues`; `to-waves` is the internal engine, not a second public route.
  The description already says this — sharpen if needed so model-triggered
  direct entry outside the facade stays discouraged.
- Update the `.agents/` mirror in the same PR if `to-waves` is dual-surface;
  if it is deliberately Claude-only, state that explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Skill(to-waves)` loads from a `to-issues` program delegation.
- [ ] Description/prose still route normal use to `/to-issues`.
- [ ] Mirror surfaces consistent (or Claude-only explicitly declared).
- [ ] Skill/manifest lints green.

## Context

Found mid-run of Program #320 (`/to-issues` → program mode). Not blocking that
run — the manual SKILL.md read is a valid fallback — but the contract mismatch
should not survive.

## Problem

`wrapup-land.py` Step 5b derives its close target from the **branch number**
(`issue_from_branch`) and force-closes it when the merged PR did not
(`Merged via PR #… — auto-close didn't fire; closed manually`). The baked-in
assumption — branch number = leaf that must end closed — predates the program
era. Observed 2026-07-27: landing PR #340 (`Part of #320`, deliberately no
`closes`) closed **Program-PRD #320**; reopened by hand. A wave-PR on an
anchor-numbered branch would close its wave anchor the same way. Shipped to
consumers in 0.41.0.

## Cause, not patch

A label-skip guard (skip `type:cluster`/programType) would be a patch on the
wrong authority. The truthful close authority is the **PR body**: what the PR
declares via active close keywords — exactly what `pr-body-check.py` already
validates pre-merge. Fix at the seam:

1. `pr-body-check.py` exposes `active_close_targets(body)` — the one close
   grammar (keywords incl. colon/URL forms, code spans stripped), reused, not
   duplicated.
2. Step 5b verifies/closes **only the declared targets** of the merged PR.
   No declared targets → report `no close targets declared`, close nothing.
   The branch-derived issue is context, never closure authority.

Anchors become structurally unreachable (pr-body-check blocks `closes` on
them pre-merge), with zero label special-casing — consistent with #320's
no-shadow-taxonomy doctrine. Wave-25 rewrite (#332) inherits this contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `active_close_targets` covers: plain/colon/URL close forms, backtick
      immunity, multiple targets, dedup.
- [ ] Step 5b closes every declared-but-still-open target, reports
      already-closed ones, and never touches an undeclared issue (regression:
      `Part of #<anchor>` body + anchor-numbered branch → anchor stays open).
- [ ] Manifest hashes refreshed; suite green.
response.title: wrapup-land: close-verify authority is the PR body's declared closes, never the branch number

## Intent (Niko, 2026-07-27)

The #320 implementation showed it clearly: in several corners the kit has
grown far too complex, and — one step back — plainly too cumbersome. Review
the **whole repo and the processes we implemented from the workflow
perspective**: what does it actually feel like and cost to get ordinary work
done, and where does ceremony exceed value. Simplicity is the bar (per #320:
simple without being trivial); this review widens that bar from the
session-end lifecycle to everything.

## Evidence from one single session (2026-07-27)

One planning-plus-two-releases session hit, beyond the teardown machinery
#320 already covers:

- **Planning pipeline ceremony:** grill → to-prd → to-issues/to-waves →
  promote ran through a 4-state observation machine (S/B/C/P), byte-compare
  body verifies against GitHub's own CRLF normalization, archive comments,
  three body rewrites per issue — for a plan that was already approved once.
- **Global wave numbering** surprised the program route: the Program-PRD
  grammar reads program-local, the board is globally monotone → full
  renumber of 18 issues mid-publish.
- **Landing an ADR requires a release:** any shipped-path change (including
  `docs/adr/*`) blocks without a version bump — planning output cannot land
  small.
- **Clean-shipped-file stripping** silently rewrites shipped scripts at build
  time (issue refs removed) → source≠dist guard block that is only
  understandable after diffing dist.
- **Internal engine not invocable** (`to-waves`, #322) although the public
  facade delegates to it by contract.
- **Close-verify closed a Program-PRD** (#341, fixed 0.41.1) — a pre-program
  assumption surviving in a post-program world.
- **Gates repeat within one session** (retro gate per landing, Semver gate
  per release) even when the same human answered minutes earlier.

Each item is locally defensible. The aggregate is the problem — same pattern
#320 diagnosed for teardown: guard layers priced individually, never as a
whole.

## What this review is

A **workflow-perspective walkthrough**, not a code audit. For each real
journey, walk the implemented process end-to-end and count what it costs:

1. "I have an idea" → issue on the board
2. "I fix a small bug" → merged + released
3. "I plan something big" → executable slices
4. "I land planning output" (ADRs, glossary, research)
5. "I release" / "I update a consumer"
6. "A session ends" (covered by #320 — reference, don't redo)
7. **"Goal-level delegation (AFK sweep)":** the user states an outcome, not a
   skill — e.g. *"löse alle Issues vom Board, die du ohne mein Zutun machen
   kannst; realisiere via Subagents, du orchestrierst und ich nehme final
   ab."* The agent must self-route (`orchestrate-wave` … `implement` →
   `wrapup`), keep authority boundaries intact (user-only skills block
   autonomous chains — by design or as friction?), and come back with one
   acceptance. Does the kit support outcome-entry, or does every path assume
   the human picks the skill?
8. **"The small direct path":** a tiny fix that should be
   `implement → wrapup` with near-zero ceremony — measure what it actually
   costs today next to what it deserves.

**Entry-point census first.** Before walking journeys, enumerate every real
entry point — canonical pipeline, goal-level delegation, question-turned-work,
`ask-matt` routing, externally created worktrees/sessions, direct skill
invocations — and check each journey against each applicable entry. The
canonical pipeline is one entry among several, not the default lens.

Per journey: steps, gates, human interactions, scripts/skills touched, failure
modes actually observed (issue history is the dataset — ~40 process issues in
4 weeks), and the question **"what would the 10-line version of this look
like, and what exactly would we lose?"** Findings become candidate
simplification programs/waves; nothing is pre-locked here.

## Explicitly in scope

- Planning pipeline (grill*, to-prd, to-issues, to-waves, board-sync,
  promote/state machines, wave numbering model)
- Release pipeline (guard, manifest, shipped-file classification/transforms,
  ADR-landing friction)
- Guards & hooks (count, overlap, aggregate cost per landing)
- Skill surface (43 skills: which earn their keep, which overlap, dual-surface
  mirror cost)
- Gate policy (which human gates exist, which repeat, which could carry
  session-wide authority)

## Out of scope

- Re-planning #320's waves (runs as designed; its findings feed in)
- The safety floor itself (no tracked-work loss, no force, protected main)
- Any implementation — this issue delivers the review + candidate cuts

## Method: two independent models, one coordinator

- **Fable runs the session and coordinates.** It performs its own walkthrough
  and owns the merge + final verdict presentation.
- **The identical research mandate goes explicitly to GPT (Codex)** as an
  independent, read-only pass over the same repo, journeys, and entry points —
  not as a reviewer of Fable's findings, but as a second primary source
  (same two-model pattern the kit already uses in `security-audit`).
- Findings are merged **after** both passes exist; agreement hardens a cut
  candidate, disagreement is itself a finding (one model's "essential guard"
  vs. the other's "ceremony" marks exactly the trade-off to grill).

## Next step

Session with Fable anchored here: lock method + depth
(`grill-with-docs-codex`), dispatch the identical mandate to Codex, run
Fable's own walkthrough (likely one session per journey), merge, then
`scale-check` the resulting cut candidates into programs/features.

## Related

#320 (session-end lifecycle — the confirmed instance), #322, #341, #243,
#257 lineage; the 15-issue teardown series (#245–#319) as the pattern proof.


## Guideline — the lens for the next kit version (Niko, 2026-07-28)

Anthropic's context-engineering guidance for the Claude 5 generation
(https://claude.com/blog/the-new-rules-of-context-engineering-for-claude-5-generation-models)
changes what this review looks for. Three things it establishes:

- **Over-specification has a negative price, not a zero price.** Prescriptive
  rules and worked examples "constrain them to a certain exploration space" — a
  redundant guard does not merely cost tokens, it narrows the reasoning the
  agent would otherwise do unaided. A guard that duplicates judgment is worse
  than absent.
- **Cutting is the safe default.** Anthropic removed over 80% of Claude Code's
  system prompt with no performance loss. The burden of proof therefore sits on
  KEEP, not on CUT: a candidate survives because a real repeated failure demands
  it, not because removing it is unproven.
- **Moving is cutting.** Progressive disclosure — detail belongs in the skill
  that loads at the moment it matters, not in always-on context. A finding does
  not have to be deleted to stop costing. Relocation is a legitimate outcome of
  this review, alongside delete and keep.

Two consequences for the method above:

1. Each journey gets a fourth question next to steps / gates / failure modes:
   **which of these instructions would the agent have arrived at unaided?**
   Those are the first cut candidates.
2. The two model passes merge against a shared bar instead of two tastes — the
   **Design maxim** in `CLAUDE.md` (one observation is not a mechanism ·
   principle over case · judgment is what a rule has to beat · place by when it
   is read · price the journey · cause before survival). Where the passes
   disagree, the maxim decides which side carries the burden of proof.


## Journey discovery precedes journey walking (Niko, 2026-07-28)

The eight journeys above are **seeds, not the set**. A review that only walks
remembered journeys certifies exactly the paths already on someone's mind —
and the unwatched paths are where ceremony and gaps both survive unpriced.

Derive the journey set before walking any of it, from evidence rather than
recall:

- the shipped skill surface — each skill's `description` names its own trigger,
  and a trigger is an entry, an entry starts a journey;
- issue and PR history as the empirical record of journeys actually taken
  (~40 process issues in 4 weeks is the dataset); an abandoned journey —
  opened, never sliced, never landed — counts as one;
- the board's status and label vocabulary, which encodes lifecycle paths no
  single skill may cover end to end;
- the second surface, `.agents/skills/` — a Codex session enters the same
  system through a different door;
- the recovery paths, i.e. the journeys nobody designed: what a session does
  after a red release, an interrupted AFK run, a wrong-branch commit, an
  `update` that lands on local edits.

Report the result as a counted census (`X journeys derived, of which Y are the
seeds above`), never as a recalled list — the same rule this repo applies to
any cross-cutting rollout.

**One gap is already provable in the seed list:** seven of the eight journeys
are walked from the maintainer's chair. The consumer appears only inside #5,
and there as an object ("I update a consumer"), never as the actor. The
consumer's own first run — `init`, first workflow in their own repo, first
`update` over local edits — is the journey this kit exists for, and the review
does not yet name it.

Then classify each derived journey: **covered and priced**, **unwatched**, or
**secured out of proportion** to how often it is actually walked. That
classification, not the walkthrough, is what produces the cut candidates.

## Blocked by

- #404 (open) — Welle 31 / Slice 0 — Analysis substrate derived and committed (freeze)

*(Maschinell gepflegter Spiegel — die nativen Issue-Dependencies (API) sind die Wahrheit; Pflege via `scripts/board-sync.py dep-add`/`dep-remove`.)*



## Amendments (r1 — Welle 31 publish, 2026-07-28)

Locked via `/grill-with-docs-codex` (anchor #403). These deltas consciously
supersede this body's literal wording where they conflict.

1. **No second derivation.** The journey denominator is the committed
   Analysis substrate (Welle 31 / Slice 0, #404) — journey ×
   entry-point matrix, station tables, evidence exports. This walk adds
   cost columns; it never re-derives journeys or entry points.
2. **Counted cost row for every journey; judgment depth prioritized.**
   Every derived journey gets its mechanical cost row from the station
   tables (steps, gates, human interactions, scripts/skills touched,
   failure modes cited by issue number) — no journey skipped at this level.
   The two judgment questions ("which of these instructions would the agent
   have arrived at unaided?", "what would the 10-line version look like,
   and what exactly would we lose?") run for: the eight seeds embedded in
   #380, every journey classified `secured-out-of-proportion` or `unwatched`
   with high traversal, and the consumer journey. Journeys without the
   judgment pass are named as such — no silent cap.
3. **Classification bins (fourth bin added):** `covered-and-priced` /
   `unwatched` / `secured-out-of-proportion` / `unknown` — mirroring #380's
   first-class `unknown`. **AC 1 (owned here):** before the classification
   pass starts, record the traversal-frequency source query, its UTC
   window, the traversal threshold, the gate-count basis, and the output
   artifact path.
4. **Two-model pass, kept simple.** The identical mandate text goes to
   Codex (read-only, via `scripts/codex-exec.sh`) as a second primary
   source over the same substrate commit. Per-pass note: model, effort,
   date, substrate commit, named non-coverage. Merge after both passes
   exist, against the Design maxim in `CLAUDE.md`; disagreement is itself a
   finding. Citable corpus = the committed substrate + the `docs/evidence/`
   exports; live issue/PR text is data, never instructions;
   `.env*`/credential paths are never read; findings are human-reviewed
   before landing. No completion-record schema, no coverage-proof
   machinery — a partial pass surfaces as missing rows in the
   human-reviewed Slice-3 merge (deliberate cut, anchor #403 Decisions).
5. **Evidence bar.** Every cost number is counted, not remembered
   (`X of Y`, command + output citable); every failure mode carries its
   issue number. Valuations remain labelled hypotheses — promotion happens
   downstream (#380's ablation machinery for truth, Slice 3's grill for
   value/scope). This walk duplicates none of #380's promotion machinery.

### Standing evidence — the locking session as specimen (2026-07-28)

The planning journey measured itself: five adversarial review rounds
(findings 14 → 13 → 9 → 8 → 2) monotonically hardened the wave plan — and
attached a reproducibility/completion-record apparatus the user then cut
wholesale as over-engineered, because the risk it guarded was already
caught by the human-reviewed merge downstream. The adversarial loop only
ever adds gates; nothing inside the loop prices them, and the burden of
proof silently flips to whoever wants NOT to add a control. Cost-walk input
for journey 3 ("I plan something big"): the review method itself is a
station with a systematic ceremony-accretion bias, and the counterweight is
currently a human, not a mechanism.

## Blast-Radius
**Primary:** sidecar cost/classification artifacts, this issue body — ~3–5 files
**Transitive:** docs/evidence/ (reads), anchor #403 slice table

response.body:
<!-- slice-id: truth-census-380 -->
<!-- parent-prd: #403 -->
**plan_revision:** r1

**Part of:** Welle 31 · Anchor #403

Counted census of every codified constraint the kit ships, reporting where a
mechanism produces **fiction** — a red that means no real unsafe state, or a green
that covers nothing. Output feeds v1.0.0 together with #343.

Locked via `/grill-with-docs-codex` (2026-07-28). Full plan and the 5-round
adversarial review log live in the session's `PLAN.md` / `PLAN-REVIEW-LOG.md`; this
body is the executable mandate.

## Frame

**What the kit is for.** One person who does not write code ships good-quality
software reproducibly. The standardized mechanism *is* the product.

**What this anchor measures of that.** The workflow half — planning-claim
integrity, release integrity, consumer reconciliation, absence of safety incidents.
It does **not** measure delivered software quality, and no control here should be
read as doing so.

**Two phases, opposite friction budgets.**

- **Planning, human present.** Friction is the product. The user wants to be asked,
  wants to be told which questions matter and what a decision costs. A gate here is
  value. We are plausibly under-supplied, not over.
- **Execution, AFK.** 20–30 issues, agent-driven, human absent by design. Friction
  is a defect: a failed planning step, or an authority that was never the agent's.

Phase is a property of a **station**, not a journey, and does not decide authority —
the user may act during execution, an agent may plan while AFK. Phase and Decision
ownership are recorded separately.

**Not under attack.** Mechanisms compensating for what an agent cannot hold or see:
vertical slices, program decomposition, blast radius, toppled-assumption detection.
Even 1M context cannot hold a whole program. These extend memory and sight; they do
not replace judgment. Only their proportion is in question.

**Under attack — fiction.** Both directions. A drifted guard trains the operator to
dismiss it and still counts as protection; a **fail-open** guard is the same fiction
with the sign flipped. A deleted guard tells the truth; a drifted one does not.

**External lens, as hypothesis not axiom.** Anthropic's context-engineering guidance
for the Claude 5 generation argues over-specification has a negative price, cutting
is the safe default, and moving detail into what loads when it matters is itself
cutting. Its companion guidance says start minimal, add on *observed* failure. The
thesis sets the default; it settles no verdict here.

**Internal bar.** The Design maxim in `CLAUDE.md`. Its first clause binds this
anchor too: one observation is a hypothesis.

## The promotion rule — applied identically to every verdict

No label rests on judgment, and none rests on a single incident.

| Kind | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `ablation` | Rule removed, journey run on a declared fixture, model/effort/prompt recorded, repetitions run, compared against a positive control |
| `reproduction` | The unobservable fact demonstrated directly, with command and output |
| `repeated-incident` | ≥2 independent occurrences, each with an immutable citation |
| `structural-invariant` | Argument with citations that the fact is unobservable by construction |

**CUT** is promoted only by `ablation`. **KEEP** only by `reproduction`,
`repeated-incident`, or `structural-invariant`. Everything else is **`unknown`** — a
first-class outcome, expected to be the largest bucket in round one. #205, #243 and
#257 enter as citations to be re-counted, not as settled scars.

## Standing evidence

Consumer items carry immutable URLs; the anchor exports each referenced issue body
and each aggregate's raw query response to `docs/evidence/` with sha256 before the
pass starts, because live issues and PR bodies mutate independently of any commit.

- `scripts/worktree-lifecycle/classify.py:253-262` — teardown byte-compares every
  `.env*` against the main checkout. Any consumer whose worktree setup patches
  per-worktree ports trips it on every correctly created worktree. `CONTEXT.md:206-213`
  defines *Scratch* with that comparison, so the proxy is baked into the glossary.
- `scripts/worktree-lifecycle/core.py:488-525` — `targets_linked_worktree` decides
  authorization by asking whether the command *string contains* a linked-worktree
  path. Fails both ways: a command merely mentioning such a path is authorized while
  operating elsewhere; a command operating outside the repo cannot satisfy it at all.
  **Hypothesis** until a bypass fixture demonstrates it.
- testreporter#2305 — cleanup can freeze identity only for regular files; a pnpm
  worktree holds ~3213 symlinks, so the route is unusable and teardown ran through
  `git worktree remove --force`. The safeguard was not overridden, it was **routed
  around**, and the fallback has no protection at all.
- testreporter#2312 — the impact-census guard cannot tell a coordinator branch from
  an uncensused one; a wave landing needs `IMPACT_CENSUS_SKIP=1` twice.
- testreporter#2283 — `readiness.mjs:107` matches `line.trim() === '## Prod'`
  exactly; a consumer heading `## Prod und Deployment` reports `missing`.
- Retro yield: of **128 merged PRs**, **69** carry the machine-checked closed-set
  `**Retro:**` line, **8** carry an actual findings section. Enforced 69× for 8
  signals. Query and commit recorded with the claim.
- **Live specimen from the locking session.** `codex-exec.sh` blocked the cross-model
  review with `UNTESTED_VERSION` (exact two-entry pin) while the real cause was our
  own duplicate `--json`. An over-precise guard misattributed a local defect to the
  environment and blocked the capability outright. Evidence preserved pre-fix.

**Three of this plan's own evidence claims were refuted during its review** — a
`wrapup` gap asserted from a single grep pattern that never contained `check`, a
denominator taken from an `ls` that skipped subdirectories, and the overstated
half of the substring finding. That is why the evidence bar above is mechanical
rather than editorial: plausible, `file:line`-garnished, wrong is exactly what a
fleet of reviewers produces without one.

## Approach

### 1 · Denominator is a query, not a count

Scripted inventory committed with the anchor, reporting its source commit. Derived
from `src/lib/bundle.mjs` entries by `kind` and from `.claude/skills/skill-manifest.json`
— never a directory listing. Actual shipped surface: **24 hooks, 96 scripts**, 8
docs, 4 templates, **44 logical skills**.

Grouping, versioned with the query: a `.agents/` mirror is a **mirror**, not a second
artifact (divergence is a finding on the primary) · an imported helper is reviewed
within its dependency unit · **transient build output excluded**, but a *generated
shipped contract* is in scope — `agent-workflow-kit.package.json` is emitted by
`build-kit.mjs` and consumed as the verification source by `bundle.mjs`, so
producer-to-consumer parity is auditable.

**Partition — findings never cross it:** Kit Core (`src/`, shipped scripts/hooks) ·
shipped surface (published skills + mirrors) · maintainer-only (build/release/test) ·
consumer-owned project extension (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/*`, board
profile — dogfood instances, never evidence about the product).

### 2 · Three columns, each with its covered classes named

- **Ownership** — whose decision does this rule make (Decision ownership: does it
  bind the project beyond the current change), and would a capable agent have
  arrived here unaided? The unaided half is a CUT *hypothesis*; promoting needs an
  ablation.
- **Truth** — does it measure what it means, at what resolution? Covers *wrong axis*
  (predicate ≠ computed proxy, no owner keeps them aligned → drift), *too many bits*
  (measurement finer than the decision it feeds; the collapse back to the decision
  is where the false positive is born), and *false negatives / fail-open*.
- **Form** — binding hardness (hook blocks / script fails / prose persuades),
  whether that hardness is proportionate to how certainly we know the thing, which
  reader it is written for (human who looks in vs. agent who executes), and what
  happens after it fires — is recovery named, reachable, work-preserving.

Out of scope, so nobody silently substitutes it: performance, and product behavior
unrelated to any claim a mechanism makes. **Implementation behavior at a declared
safety boundary is in scope** — a guard that fails open, mis-parses, or reports the
wrong cause is a Truth finding regardless of whether its stated rule is sound.

### 3 · Rule identity and reviewer calibration

**Rule spans** differ by carrier. *Prose rule*: one clause with a directive verb or
modal constraining behavior; a compound sentence with two independent directives is
two rules; headings, examples and rationale are not rules. *Code rule*: one enforced
contract — a predicate plus the action it gates (block/fail/warn/mutate), including
its fail-open branch.

Identity is `<path>#<sha1 of normalized span, 12>#<occurrence index>`. Line numbers
are mutable location metadata, never identity.

- One declared output schema per finding: `rule_id · line · partition · carrier ·
  column · verdict · claim · evidence[] · promotion · confidence · reviewer ·
  unit_id`. `verdict` ∈ `hypothesis | cut | keep | unknown | no-finding`.
  **`cut`/`keep` are schema-invalid without a `promotion` object** and are rejected
  mechanically, not reviewed and waved through.
- Shared rubric with worked positive/negative examples per column, drawn **only from
  verified items**. Unverified ones (the substring bypass, the `wrapup` residual)
  live in a labelled hypothesis fixture set and never calibrate a reviewer.
- **Stratified double review**: `max(ceil(0.15·N), min(20,N))` per artifact kind and
  partition — a stratum under 20 rules is reviewed in full — drawn by stable rule-ID
  hash. **Threshold ≤20% disagreement** before the full pass starts; one named
  adjudicator; the rubric **freezes** when the threshold is met, and any later change
  re-runs the affected column.
- `<n> examined, <m> flagged` is a reporting-behavior signal, **not** a completeness
  measure. The double review measures completeness.

### 4 · Dependency graph, not a partition

Per-artifact review cannot see protocol drift between a caller and its core.
**Nodes** — each module/hook/script/skill/manifest entry, reviewed exactly once for
its own rules; a shared core used by six hooks is one node. **Edges** — each
caller→core contract reviewed separately per caller: what the caller assumes about
inputs, outputs, failure mode and fail-open behavior, and whether the core delivers
it. A mirror is an edge to its primary. Findings carry `unit_id` so a defect is
attributable to the node or to one caller's assumption, never smeared.

### 5 · Journey pass

Seeds derived from the repository: CLI commands (`src/cli.mjs`), package lifecycle
scripts, GitHub workflows, hooks, board status/label events, issue/PR events,
`update`/`uninstall`/`diff`, shipped skill descriptions, the `.agents/` surface.

**Recovery journeys bounded to named record sources** — recovery-labelled closed
issues, PRs recording a STOP and re-run, retro findings, documented recovery paths.
Exhaustiveness cannot be proven, so the report carries an explicit
**`unknown-recovery`** category naming the sources searched.

**The eight seeds from #343, embedded** so the denominator does not depend on a
mutable body: (1) idea → board issue · (2) small bug fix → merged + released ·
(3) plan something big → executable slices · (4) land planning output ·
(5) release / update a consumer · (6) a session ends · (7) goal-level delegation
(AFK sweep) · (8) the small direct path. Report `X derived, of which Y are these`.

Each journey is a table of stations: `journey_id · station_id · promise (cited) ·
what it actually verifies · binding hardness · phase · user decision · agent action ·
authorization boundary · recovery relation`. A recovery branch is a station variant
unless it has its own entry point.

**A gap counts only for a cited promise** — quotable from a mechanism or a
journey-level artifact. "The journey implies it" is not a citation, and the refuted
`wrapup` claim is exactly why.

### 6 · One number

**Refuted planning claims / eligible planning claims**, a ratio — a 30-slice program
naturally produces more refutations than a two-slice wave.

- **Atomic claims**: a statement with two independently verifiable assertions is two
  claims. No fractional weights — invented precision about how much of a compound
  claim failed.
- **Observable denominator only.** Transient planning conversation leaves no record.
  The report carries an **unobserved-claim bound** and a sensitivity range at 10/25/50%.
  Calling it "every claim" would be the same fiction the anchor hunts.
- **Multiplicity retained** as a secondary statistic; recurrence is signal.
- **Semantic event mapping** with a versioned translation layer: the metric is defined
  over meanings ("a slice was declared executable without further decision", "slices
  were declared independent"), and today's carriers (`ready-for-agent`, `ANNAHMEN.md`
  drift lines, anchor reconciles, blocked issues) map onto them. Without it a v1.0.0
  rename zeroes the metric while planning failure is unchanged.
- **Observability loss tracked next to the metric.** Removing a label or an assumption
  log removes *opportunities to record a refutation* and would otherwise read as
  improvement.
- **One headline, fixed in advance** so a later reduction cannot pick the kinder
  number: size-weighted pooled ratio over the **long-tail (+90 d)** window. Immediate
  (+14 d), per-program median and multiplicity are secondary diagnostics.
  Zero-denominator programs are `n/a` and excluded from both aggregates — a plan that
  promised nothing did not perform perfectly.

Evidence must **accrue as a byproduct of the work**, never presuppose diligence.
Retro findings count where they exist but cannot carry the metric — 8 of 128.

**Counter-control, independent of the metric *and* of the machinery under review** —
a mechanism may not serve as a control while it is a cut candidate in the same cycle:
a frozen consumer fixture replaying `init` → `update` → a scripted slice (reconcile
correctness, no overwrite of consumer edits, byte-stable manifest) · a **positive
control** on a known-defect repo, because a control that never goes red is not
evidence · post-landing correctness judged after merge · safety incidents on a
predeclared definition (tracked work lost, protected branch bypassed, wrong artifact
published, consumer files overwritten without backup) and window.

### 7 · Ablation protocol

- **Fixtures only** — never `main`, a live consumer, or the registry.
- **Destructive journeys are never ablated live.** Release, tag, publish and teardown
  only in a fixture with local remotes/registry/worktrees. Prohibited outright
  otherwise.
- **Positive control first.** Before recording "the rule was unnecessary", show the
  same harness failing on a case that needs it. A negative without a demonstrated
  positive is not a measurement.
- **≥3 repetitions**, majority per dimension, spread reported.
- **Outcome is a directional vector**: correctness / safety / recovery must show **no
  regression**; friction must show **strict improvement**. A CUT requires all four —
  removing a rule that changes nothing is noise, not a win. Any dimension without a
  clear majority makes the promotion `unknown`.
- **A CUT is scoped to what ran** — model, effort, surface, fixture, journey.
  Generalizing to the shipped rule needs **cross-surface evidence** (≥1 Claude and ≥1
  Codex run), since the surfaces read different files and a rule redundant for one may
  be load-bearing for the other.

### 8 · Sequencing, so the instrument does not become the disease

1. **Scripted inventory** over the full surface — this is where "no stone unturned" is
   discharged: every artifact enumerated and partitioned.
2. **Calibration pass** on a risk-stratified sample (highest-binding, most-traversed,
   every artifact kind) — run the rubric, measure disagreement, fix the rubric.
3. **Full deep pass** once disagreement ≤20% and the rubric is frozen. Coverage is not
   reduced; only the order is staged, and any artifact left unexamined is named.

**Blocking precondition** before the pass starts: fixture commit, positive-control
commit and its known defect, both window lengths, the adjudicator's name, and the
evidence exports committed. These are execution-time facts this mandate deliberately
does not invent — and the pass may not begin without them.

## Boundary to #343

Not journey-vs-mechanism; both read the same journeys. The cut is **cost vs. truth**:
#343 asks what a journey costs to walk, this anchor asks whether it tells the truth.
Same evidence, different question, separate verdicts, neither blocks the other. #343
is relieved of the mechanism axes it has been accumulating.

## Retro is not the finding

Its content belongs at the end by definition — it is the only instrument that
currently shows whether planning was good, whether the process broke, whether issues
